opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; write is at the maximum for this role, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E023 is a contractor with basic training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting employment information: the HR note lists E023 as a full-time Engineer (max write), while the Security note states E023 is a contractor with basic security training (max read). Per policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read, and never admin. Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive classification: contractor with basic training, whose maximum is read. The requested write exceeds this maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed: read.

1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Engineer doesn't own Payroll.

- If contractor with basic training: max read. Requested write exceeds → grant read.
